title: openObsControlChannel().close() does nothing before the handshake completes, leaving the channel open for the page lifetime
test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'closing the OBS control channel while it is still connecting closes the socket for good' (VAL-110), 'closing the OBS control channel while it authenticates closes the socket and never identifies', 'closing the OBS control channel right behind Identified never runs the channel setup'; guard: 'closing the OBS control channel twice, or after it opened, still settles ready once' (passed before and after)
proof: Holds. close() could end the connection only through settleConnection, which the callback assigned after Identified (op 2); before that it only nulled sendRequest, so the socket stayed open, ready never resolved as a failure, and the handshake that completed later ran the callback, re-armed sendRequest and resolved ready with success. The tests drive a hand-fed fake socket (it records every frame written and the close) and call close() before the handshake. On the unchanged code: the VAL-110 test failed at 'close() has to end a socket that has not identified yet' (false !== true: the fake socket was not closed); the authentication test failed at ws.closed (false !== true) with the password hash still being computed; the right-behind-Identified test failed the same way (false !== true). After the fix all pass, and mutation checks show each guard matters: without the post-hash settled check the late identify frame is written to the closed socket (authentication test fails), without the settled check before the callback the channel opens and ready resolves with success (right-behind-Identified test fails). Fix: withObsConnection returns its promise with an abort(result) method that settles through done at any stage (closes the socket, rejects pending requests, clears timers; a no-op once settled). The WebSocket message handler ignores everything once the transaction has settled, does not send the identify frame if the transaction ended while the password hash was computed, and the callback is not run if the transaction settled between Identified and the callback's turn. openObsControlChannel().close() now calls connection.abort(): { success: true, 'OBS control channel closed.' } when the channel was open, { success: false, 'OBS control channel closed before it opened.' } otherwise, which is what ready then resolves with when it had not resolved yet (ready resolves exactly once). stopStream() resolves false after close; on an open channel it still writes one frame immediately (existing test unchanged and passing).
